issue_context.title: EventSource source generator should mark both source and IL as autogenerated
issue_context.body:
Per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/64541, it should emit `<autogenerated>` into the source and also `[GeneratedCodeAttribute...]` for the IL. 

Our other generators do this; this enables tooling and servicing scenarios.

eg regex generator
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/9df283248256dd880eb1ee5ecce533ad206a55d3/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/gen/RegexGenerator.Emitter.cs#L27-L31

review_comments: maybe not worth having an array you loop over unless we have more than one thing? perhaps just append the string on line 41.

I copied it from the Regex source generator. It is more extensible in case we want to suppress warnings in the future, and isn't particularly heavy performance-wise (a `foreach` loop over an array will be translated to a simple `for` loop).

We can still have it extensible and still using one string.

```C#

"// <auto-generated/>" + Environment.NewLine +
"any future string"    + Environment.NewLine + 
Environment.NewLine;
```

I agree it is not perf critical though :-)

Extensible is good when it means we can make future changes less disruptively. In this case, it's private code; we can do whatever we want. 😸 Similarly we don't have a string[] for assembly attributes here, as we just have one, nor for using statements.

I would just append the line as you do the attribute.
